scenario.description: A collateral management director must decide whether to authorize a partial release of pledged warehouse inventory so a borrower can complete a sale, and must set the release amount, cash paydown, legal controls, and post-release monitoring plan with input from risk, legal, relationship management, and collateral operations.

shared_context.S1: The borrower has $4,000,000 of packaged inventory pledged under the bank's working-capital facility.
shared_context.S2: The borrower has requested release of inventory worth $2,500,000 so it can complete a contracted customer sale.
shared_context.S3: The facility is current, and the warehouse receipts are held in the bank's collateral-control process.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding collateral-release decision.
shared_context.S5: The bank's routine collateral review requires risk, legal, relationship management, and collateral operations to report relevant findings before Maya finalizes a release.
shared_context.S6: For any approved release, the collateral file must contain written sign-offs from risk, legal, relationship management, and collateral operations before the warehouse acts.
shared_context.S7: The release memorandum must record each function's written finding before the warehouse acts.

PF1.text: Jonah's borrowing-base review completed this week shows that policy permits release of only $1,500,000 of this inventory, provided the borrower makes a cash paydown of exactly $1,800,000; the review is still in his working paper and has not been circulated.

PF2.text: Elena confirmed in a legal review memo received yesterday that every inventory release requires dual bank authorization and a signed lien-release letter before the warehouse receipt is handed over; she has not yet attached the memo to the release file.

PF3.text: The borrower has confirmed to Ravi that its customer will transfer exactly $1,800,000 to the bank on the release date, and the borrower has authorized that amount to be applied as the required paydown; Ravi recorded this in a client call note this morning that has not reached collateral management.

PF4.text: Tessa verified with the warehouse this morning that, after the release, the remaining pledged inventory can be physically inspected weekly and a Friday inventory report can be delivered; operations can enforce both controls, but the capability is not yet reflected in the standard release checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The collateral release must be authorized.
The released inventory value must be exactly $1,500,000.
The borrower must make exactly $1,800,000 of cash paydown on the release date.
Dual bank authorization and a signed lien-release letter must both be required before the warehouse receipt is handed over.
Weekly physical inspection and a Friday inventory report must both be required for the remaining pledged inventory.
The settlement must include commitments documenting the confirmed cash paydown, the legal release controls, and the post-release monitoring controls.

content_checks.C6: 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and decisions['cash_paydown_usd'] == 1800000 and decisions['release_authorized'] == True
content_checks.C7: 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and any(('lien-release letter' in c['detail'] or 'lien release' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and any(('weekly physical inspection' in c['detail'] or 'Friday inventory report' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The public request is for $2,500,000 with no specified paydown; PF1 changes released_inventory_value_usd to exactly $1,500,000 and cash_paydown_usd to exactly $1,800,000.
The public file contains no special execution controls; PF2 changes both legal decisions to true and requires a commitment whose detail documents the lien-release letter.

Without PF3, the required $1,800,000 paydown has no confirmed source and the release should not be authorized; PF3 confirms that the customer's exactly $1,800,000 transfer is authorized for the paydown.

The public facts provide no post-release monitoring plan; PF4 changes both monitoring decisions to true and requires a commitment documenting the weekly physical inspection or Friday inventory report.
